title: Everest Boogie: his bass line credited to Joe Avery
summary: His bass figure became Everest Boogie, named for Joe Avery; he earned only a few dollars and believes it should be Tillman Boogie.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Oh, that wasn't enough for the bar staff to put on a letter. My Me Good, the highest My Me Got was around $3.36. Is that all? That's right. Hmm. You're getting a check for $3.36 and $3.30 and $3.40, that ain't no kind of royalty to get off no record. Like that, that record is still selling yet. Yeah. And I'm the one should have been drawing the royalty on that because I'm the one made up the piece, but I didn't, instead of me saying Tillman Boogie, I told him this artist called it Everest Boogie.
Oh, that Joe Everest piece you made that up? That was my number.

We made that number up during the other time. We was playing a few of them called them. And I made, that's the first time I made that hoop on the base. And Joe looked at me and said, you got something new? He said, well you learned that. I said, that's all right. He said, well what you don't name that? I said, I'm going to name it after you. I'm going to call it Everest Boogie. But it should have been named Tillman Boogie because then nobody knows nothing about it. And they had a bass player in the whole city of New York and can play it like me right now. None of them didn't all try. Joshua didn't try. Because I don't know what I'm going to make on it myself until I make it.
